newsitem.title: FRANCE: Billboard firm Dauphin Q1 sales up 12 pct.
newsitem.headline: Billboard firm Dauphin Q1 sales up 12 pct.

text.p: French billboard advertising company Dauphin's turnover rose 12 percent in the first quarter to the end of March, due largely to growth in Spain and Italy, Dauphin chairman Jacques Machurot said on Friday.
But he told a news conference that he did not expect that pace of growth to continue throughout the year.
"It's a good start to the year. Which doesn't mean we will continue at that pace this year. We are ahead for the period. We are not going to complain," Machurot said.
Overall turnover should rise 4.5 percent by the end of June, as order books are full to that date, he said.
Dauphin has budgeted for growth of two percent this year, although the billboard advertising market should grow four percent over the year, he said.

Dauphin's turnover rose seven percent in France in the first quarter, with the domestic market up 12 percent thanks to advertising for telecommunications, food products, luxury items and fashion, he said.
The imminent part-privatisation of France Telecom and tariff-cutting by the three mobile telephone operators have boosted advertising by telecommunications firms.
If there are early elections in France in June, this would have only a limited impact on Dauphin's business, since there are firm bookings on billboards up to that date, he said.
Speculation is rife in France that President Jacques Chirac might call early Parliamentary elections, although these are not due until next year.

In Spain, Dauphin's turnover rose 15 percent to the end of March, while in Italy growth was 30 percent in the same period, he said. On the same trend, by the end of June Dauphin's Spanish activities will show a rise of 10 percent and its Italian business a rise of 15 percent, he added.
Dauphin, France's biggest billboard company, posted a 46 percentg rise in net attributable profit in 1996 to 61.9 million francs, on turnover 21.3 percent higher at 1.36 billion francs.
It has said it will pay an increased dividend of 5.40 francs net, up from 5.10 francs in 1995.
